subcommands.name: intro
subcommands.short: Teach Claude about SDF and save a skill for future sessions
subcommands.long:
Spawns Claude as a child process, introduces SDF (rules, commands,
workflows), and asks Claude to create a skill file so it remembers how
to use SDF in future sessions. Claude's output streams to the terminal.

commands.short: Add a new branch to the current stack

flags.name: stack
flags.description: stack to add the branch to (default: auto-detect)

commands.name: completion
commands.short: Generate or install shell completion scripts
commands.long:
Generate shell completion scripts for sdf.

To load completions manually:

  Bash:
    $ sdf completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/sdf

  Zsh:
    $ sdf completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_sdf"

  Fish:
    $ sdf completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/sdf.fish

  PowerShell:
    PS> sdf completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

Or use 'sdf completion install' to auto-detect your shell and install.

subcommands.name: install
subcommands.short: Auto-detect shell and install completion scripts
subcommands.long:
Detects your current shell from $SHELL and writes completions to
the standard location so they load automatically in new sessions.

Supported shells: bash, zsh, fish.

subcommands.name: set
subcommands.example:
sdf config set branch_prefix.enabled true
  sdf config set --global pr_title.conventional_commits true

commands.name: doctor
commands.long: Reports the status of git (required), gh (needed for PR operations), and claude (needed for conflict resolution and PR descriptions).

commands.name: fetch
commands.short: Discover and sync PR stacks from GitHub
commands.long:
Scans your open PRs, detects branch chains, and either registers
a new stack or reconciles an existing one.
commands.example:
sdf fetch                          # auto-detect base, scan all open PRs
  sdf fetch --stack my-feature       # name the stack explicitly
  sdf fetch --base develop           # specify base branch

flags.name: stack
flags.description: name for the stack (default: auto-generated from branches)

commands.name: merge
commands.short: Merge head PR and sync remaining branches
commands.long:
Merges the first open PR in the stack, retargets the next PR's base,
then triggers a sync to cascade-rebase remaining branches.
commands.example:
sdf merge                          # merge with squash (default)
  sdf merge -y                       # skip confirmation
  sdf merge --method merge           # use regular merge
  sdf merge --stack my-feature       # target a specific stack

flags.name: method
flags.description: merge method: squash, merge, or rebase

commands.name: move
commands.short: Move commits from current branch to parent
commands.long:
Cherry-picks listed commits onto the parent branch, strips them from the
current branch via rebase, and cascade-rebases downstream branches.
commands.example:
sdf move abc1234                   # move one commit
  sdf move abc1234 def5678           # move multiple commits

commands.name: new
commands.short: Create a new stack and its first branch
commands.long:
The stack name can be provided as a positional argument or via the --stack flag.
If --branch is omitted, the first branch is named after the stack. The base branch
is auto-detected from origin HEAD if not specified.
commands.example:
sdf new my-feature                                # positional stack name
  sdf new --stack my-feature                        # explicit flag
  sdf new my-feature --branch db-schema             # custom first branch name
  sdf new my-feature --base develop                 # custom base branch
  sdf new my-feature --json                         # machine-readable output

commands.name: split
commands.short: Split a branch into a stack of smaller PRs
commands.long:
Uses an AI agent to analyze a branch and decompose it into a chain of
focused, reviewable PRs managed as an sdf stack.

Requires the Claude CLI to be installed. The original branch is never modified.
commands.example:
sdf split --from feature/big-change --stack my-feature
  sdf split --from feature/big-change --stack my-feature --dry-run
  sdf split --from feature/big-change --stack my-feature --base main -y

flags.name: dry-run
flags.description: show the split plan without executing

flags.name: no-push

commands.name: status
commands.short: Show stack topology and sync state

commands.name: switch
commands.short: Switch to a branch and report its stack
commands.long:
Without arguments, lists all branches across all stacks.
With a branch name, checks it out and shows its stack position.
commands.example:
sdf switch db-schema              # switch to a specific branch
  sdf switch                        # list all branches from all stacks

commands.name: sync
commands.short: Detect merged PRs and cascade-rebase downstream branches
commands.long:
Fetches from origin, queries GitHub for PR status, reconciles PR states,
cascade-rebases downstream branches, pushes, and updates PR navigation links.

By default, sync only rebases branches within the stack (e.g. after a PR is
merged or a parent branch is amended). To also rebase onto the latest base
branch tip (e.g. main), use --from-head.

When a rebase conflict occurs, an interactive menu offers Claude resolution,
manual resolution (pausing sync), skip, or abort.
commands.example:
sdf sync                          # sync within the stack only
  sdf sync --from-head              # also rebase onto latest base branch
  sdf sync my-feature               # sync a specific stack by name
  sdf sync -y                       # skip confirmation prompt
  sdf sync --continue               # resume after manual conflict resolution
  sdf sync --with-content           # also update PR titles and descriptions

flags.name: from-head
flags.description: also rebase onto the latest base branch
